attribution: Existing CSS Vista Essay Themes 2027 research roadmap; preserve its research directions and source-verification requirements.

stages.title: 1 · Understand the theme
stages.teach: Read the actual roadmap brief. State the central issue, a boundary and a question within that boundary. The roadmap gives research directions; it does not establish that every listed claim is true.
stages.example: For a broad access theme, studying a specific barrier can be within scope; a disconnected personal preference may not be.
stages.question: Explain the theme in two simple sentences. Name one issue that belongs within it.

stages.title: 2 · Brainstorm
stages.teach: Generate your own ideas. Connect each to the theme and identify at least one idea that should be excluded. Beginners: start with who is affected, how and why. Intermediate: consider institutions and alternatives. Advanced: examine conditions and trade-offs.
stages.example: An access proposal could raise questions about timing, resources and unequal effects; those are questions for research, not proven findings.
stages.question: Who is affected, what difficulty might they face, and why does it belong to this theme?

stages.title: 3 · Develop a thesis
stages.teach: A theme is a topic; a thesis is a defensible central argument about it. State your position, reasoning direction and necessary qualification. Use the actual theme, not a generic slogan.
stages.example: A trial can be defended under specified conditions without claiming it will solve every problem.
stages.question: What do you think about one issue within the theme, and what is your main reason?

stages.title: 4 · Construct arguments
stages.teach: Develop a claim, reason and relevant support. Mark the evidence you still need. You can send this saved work to the Argumentation Builder and explicitly bring its revision back.
stages.example: Explain why the reason supports the thesis rather than adding an unrelated impressive quotation.
stages.question: Write one claim, explain your reason, and name the evidence you would need.

stages.title: 5 · Analyse critically
stages.teach: Examine a mechanism, competing view, limitation and implication. Use the Analytical Builder to strengthen your own analysis without replacing your essay record.
stages.example: A plausible explanation still needs an alternative explanation and a way to distinguish them.
stages.question: What is one possible objection, and when might your proposed answer fail?

stages.title: 6 · Build an outline
stages.teach: Organise your thesis, main headings, arguments, evidence needs and conclusion. Check relevance, sequence, overlap and balance. Each heading needs a clear job.
stages.example: A useful outline separates the central claim, supporting reasoning, serious objection and qualified conclusion.
stages.question: Arrange your thesis, two different reasons, an objection and a conclusion into headings.

stages.title: 7 · Practise and revise
stages.teach: Write an independent paragraph or essay draft based on your outline. Review organisation, logic, expression and coherence. Saved revisions preserve earlier versions; optional AI feedback is formative and cannot change human mentor marks.
stages.example: After drafting, check whether each paragraph advances the thesis and whether factual support is actually verified.
stages.question: Write one paragraph from your outline in your own words.

title: Palestine, International Law & Crisis of Global Governance
explanation: Build a legal-institutional and humanitarian research file that clearly separates verified facts, legal questions, court findings or orders, state positions and contested political claims.
example: Use the research directions to formulate questions. They are not a supplied thesis or a verified evidence bank.
task: Develop your own thesis and outline within Palestine, International Law & Crisis of Global Governance.

items.text: Build a carefully sourced timeline from late Ottoman/British Mandate background through UN partition debates, wars, occupation and peace-process milestones.
Trace the evolution of the Palestinian question in UN organs and international courts.
Separate major wars and territorial changes from later settlement, blockade and peace-process developments.
Build a timeline of relevant ICJ/ICC proceedings using official court documents only.
Track humanitarian and displacement developments using UN agencies, clearly date-stamping every figure.
Security Council veto and institutional legitimacy
